docs.title: UB AI Physics
docs.text:
Physics teaching material made by volunteer students of the Physics degree at the University of Barcelona, with the help of Claude.

  • Lecture notes

    Notes for physics courses, from first to fourth year.

  • Simulations

    Interactive web pages and animations that show a physical effect.

  • Solved problems

    Worked-out exercises, with figures.

  • Contribute

    How to add your own work, step by step. No GitHub experience needed.

Work in progress

This is our shared workspace, not a finished product. Pages marked draft have not been reviewed yet.

The project is coordinated by students and supervised by Vincent Mathieu. Communication happens on Campus Virtual; see the Team page.

docs.title: Contribute
docs.text: Everything here can be done in your web browser. You don't need to install anything or know git.

docs.title: How it works in one minute
docs.text:
• The website is built from the files in our GitHub repository, ub-ai-physics/ub-ai-physics.github.io.
  • When you change or add a file, GitHub does not publish it straight away. It creates a proposal (GitHub calls it a pull request).
  • A coordinator reads the proposal, may leave comments, and clicks Merge. A minute or two later the website is updated.
  • Every change keeps your name, and anything can be undone. You can't break the site.

docs.title: Before your first contribution
docs.text:
1. Create a free account at github.com/signup. Tip: as a student you can also ask for the free GitHub Student Developer Pack.
  2. Post your GitHub username on Campus Virtual. A coordinator will invite you to the ub-ai-physics organization.
  3. Accept the invitation (you get it by email, or at github.com/ub-ai-physics).

docs.title: Fix or improve an existing page
docs.text:
1. On the website, open the page and click the pencil icon at the top right of the text.
  2. Make your change in the editor. The Preview tab shows how it looks.
  3. Click Commit changes…, write one line saying what you changed, choose Create a new branch and start a pull request, then click Propose changes.
  4. On the next screen click Create pull request. Done: the coordinators are notified.

docs.title: Add lecture notes or a solved problem
docs.text:
1. Ask Claude to write your notes in Markdown with LaTeX math (for example: "Write these notes as a Markdown file. Use \( \) for inline math and \[ \] for displayed equations.").
  2. In the repository, open the folder docs/notes/ (or docs/problems/), click Add file → Create new file.
  3. Name the file in lowercase with dashes, for example rigid-body-rotation.md.

  4. Start the file with the block below, filled in, then paste your text after it. The example notes show the whole format.

    ---
title: "Rigid body rotation"
author: Your Name
course: Mechanics
year: 1
status: draft
tags:
  - Mechanics
  - Year 1
---

  5. Add a line for your page to the table on the section's main page (docs/notes/index.md or docs/problems/index.md), in the same proposal if you can, or in a second one.

  6. Click Commit changes… and propose the change as above.

Images: upload them next to your page (Add file → Upload files) and show them with ![Short description](my-figure.png).

docs.title: Add a simulation or animation
docs.text:
1. Ask Claude for a single HTML file with everything inside (no separate CSS or JS files, no data to download), so it works anywhere.
  2. In the repository, open docs/simulations/, click Add file → Upload files, and drag your file in. In the file name box at the top, type a folder name before it so the path becomes docs/simulations/coriolis/index.html.
  3. Add a line to the table in docs/simulations/index.md, then propose the change.

docs.title: Using Claude Code instead
docs.text: If you use Claude Code on your computer, you can ask it to do all of this for you: "Clone github.com/ub-ai-physics/ub-ai-physics.github.io, add my notes as a new page following docs/contribute.md, and open a pull request."

docs.title: Status of a page
docs.text:
• draft: written, not yet checked by someone else.
  • reviewed: another student (or the supervisor) has checked the physics. The reviewer changes the status and adds their name.

docs.title: For coordinators
docs.text:
• Check the open proposals in the Pull requests tab. Read the Files changed tab, leave comments if needed, then Approve and Merge.
  • After merging, the Actions tab shows the site being rebuilt. If it turns red, the build log says which file has a problem.
  • Keep the tables on the section pages up to date, and move pages into course subfolders when a section grows.

docs.title: Simple harmonic oscillator (example)
docs.text:
About this page

Author: Example Student · Course: Mechanics · Year: 1 · Status: draft

This is an example to copy. Replace the text, keep the block at the top of the file (between the --- lines) and fill it in.

docs.title: Equation of motion
docs.text:
A mass \(m\) attached to a spring of constant \(k\) obeys Newton's second law:

\[ m\,\ddot{x} = -k\,x . \]

With \(\omega = \sqrt{k/m}\), the general solution is

\[ x(t) = A\cos(\omega t + \varphi), \]

where the amplitude \(A\) and the phase \(\varphi\) are fixed by the initial conditions.

docs.title: Energy
docs.text:
The total energy is conserved:

\[ E = \tfrac12 m\dot{x}^2 + \tfrac12 k x^2 = \tfrac12 k A^2 . \]

docs.title: See it move
docs.text: Open the pendulum simulation: for small angles the pendulum is a harmonic oscillator with \(\omega = \sqrt{g/L}\).

About this page

Author: Example Student · Course: Mechanics · Year: 1 · Status: draft

docs.title: Statement
docs.text:
A block of mass \(m\) slides down a plane inclined at an angle \(\theta\), with kinetic friction coefficient \(\mu\). Find its acceleration.

m θ

A figure can be an image file or an SVG drawn by Claude, like this one.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Along the plane, the forces are the component of the weight \(mg\sin\theta\) and friction \(\mu N\), with \(N = mg\cos\theta\). Newton's second law gives

\[ m a = mg\sin\theta - \mu\, mg\cos\theta \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a = g\,(\sin\theta - \mu\cos\theta). \] Check

The block only slides if \(a > 0\), that is if \(\tan\theta > \mu\).
